results.title: The Healthcare Payer's Algorithm — VI : AI-Powered Fraud ...
results.content: # The Healthcare Payer’s Algorithm — VI : AI-Powered Fraud, Waste, and Abuse (FWA) Detection. ## Moving beyond reactive “pay-and-chase” methods to a sophisticated pre-payment prevention model, this analysis details how anomaly detection and network graph analytics deliver a demonstrable ROI by stopping fraudulent activity before it impacts the bottom line. > tl;dr — AI is revolutionizing healthcare by shifting the fight against fraud from a reactive “pay-and-chase” model to a proactive, real-time prevention strategy. By leveraging machine learning, generative AI, and autonomous agents to analyze vast datasets, payers can now detect and stop sophisticated scams before payment, saving billions of dollars, protecting patients from harm, and augmenting human investigators to focus on the most complex threats. The sheer scale of fraud, waste, and abuse is no longer just a cost of doing business in U.S. healthcare; it’s a multi-hundred-billion-dollar hemorrhage that inflates premiums and erodes trust. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.

results.title: Hybrid deep learning-enabled framework for enhancing ...
results.content: These are reflective of the lack of an end-to-end integrated, trust-aware deep learning model that can conduct secure, trustworthy, and efficient processing of health data in real-time edge-based H-IoT networks. As illustrated in Fig. 1, the system consists of four intertwined modules: (i) a CNN-driven spatial anomaly detection module that operates directly on raw physiological signals, (ii) an LSTM-driven temporal analysis module that identifies sequential patterns and marks predictive threats, (iii) a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) module that reconstructs input signals and identifies tampering through reconstruction loss, and (iv) a Trust-Aware Adaptive Controller (TAC) that scans device reliability scores based on history data and model confidence. The major goal of the introduced hybrid deep learning model is to optimize multi-objective outcomes of Healthcare Internet of Things (H-IoT) systems in parallel while they improve security, maintain data integrity, and ensure real-time performance. The current study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning architecture merging CNN-LSTM and VAE models with a decision controller that is trust-aware for ensuring security for real-time H-IoT systems.
